openQuestions: US-R6-001 (CAM-488) is structurally undoable by an implementer session: the fix is a text edit to scripts/cam/prd.json's own acceptanceCriteria oracle strings (US-001 AC1-AC3, US-002 AC1-AC5/AC7), and .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh denies Write/Edit/MultiEdit against *scripts/cam/prd.json whenever CAM_WORKER=1 (confirmed set this session via `env`). This is the same structural dead end already recorded at scripts/cam/patterns.md:1058-1074 (CAM-433/CAM-434): per that precedent's own rule, do not narrate the red Layer B oracle green or route around the hook via a raw Bash write (would defeat the guard's purpose of stopping a worker from self-grading its own acceptance criteria) -- halt, emit BLOCKED_QUALITY, and hand the exact edit to a planner/reviewer/operator session.

Root cause (re-verified empirically this session, not just re-read from the finding): US-R2-001 made runGates async (scripts/check-all.ts) but 8 of these 9 directives call `runGates({...})` WITHOUT `await` and read the log/rows array on the very next synchronous statement, so they observe an empty array before any gate has run -- reproduced live: US-001 AC1 unmodified prints 'RED suite=' (verbatim match to the finding); the SAME oracle text with `await runGates(...)` and an `async (c, a) => {...}` fake spawnFn prints GREEN (verified for all 9 below).

Exact ready-to-paste fix for each of the 9 oracle strings (verified GREEN against current branch HEAD by running each one for real; only the two shown edits are needed per directive -- add `await` before `runGates(` and make the fake spawnFn `async` -- EXCEPT US-001 AC2 and US-002 AC3, noted separately):
prd.json US-001 AC1 -- in the oracle string, change `runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => {` to `await runGates({ spawnFn: (async (c, a) => {`. Verified GREEN.

prd.json US-001 AC2 -- NOT a mechanical await-fix: it prints GREEN today only incidentally (the SENTINELOUT/SENTINELERR markers land inside the skip-ratchet gate's own 'Raw output (first 300 chars):' failure-message dump, verified this session: unmodified oracle output ends '...Raw output (first 300 chars): SENTINELOUTSENTINELERR' then 'GREEN'). After US-R2-001 the real echo/tee lives only inside runStreamingSuiteGate (scripts/check-all.ts:276-298), reached only via the DEFAULT spawnFn (:392-398) -- a fake-injected spawnFn structurally bypasses that path entirely, so no fake-spawn oracle can ever test the real tee again, even a correctly-awaited one. Recommend retargeting AC2's oracle at the dedicated unit coverage already added for this in US-R2-001: `[oracle: bun test test/check-all-streaming.test.ts]` -- verified this session: exits 0, 3 pass/0 fail, and (per the file not existing pre-US-R2-001) would have been red-on-main exactly like AC4's shape. A planner/reviewer should confirm this retarget captures the AC's original intent (live tee, not post-hoc replay) before pasting it in; this is a judgment call, not a mechanical fix, hence flagged separately from the 8 below.
prd.json US-001 AC3 -- change `runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => ({` to `await runGates({ spawnFn: (async (c, a) => ({`. Verified GREEN.
prd.json US-002 AC1 -- identical mechanical fix as US-001 AC1 (same log-filter shape). Verified GREEN.
prd.json US-002 AC2 -- change `runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => {` to `await runGates({ spawnFn: (async (c, a) => {`. Verified GREEN.

prd.json US-002 AC3 -- mechanical fix PLUS a structural change: the oracle's `blobs.map((b) => {...})` callback must become a `for (const b of blobs) { ... }` loop (an async arrow inside `.map` would return a Promise per element instead of sequencing the awaits), pushing into a `verdicts` array declared before the loop, then `await runGates(...)` inside the loop body with an `async` fake spawnFn. Verified GREEN with this shape; a plain mechanical await-inside-map edit would NOT work (untested, but `.map` with async callbacks not awaited by `.map` itself is a well-known JS foot-gun -- verified by construction, not run, since the correct for-loop form was used directly).

prd.json US-002 AC4 -- change the `run = (code, blob) => {` helper to `run = async (code, blob) => {`, `runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => {` to `await runGates({ spawnFn: (async (c, a) => {`, and both call sites `const a = run(1, good); const b = run(0, under);` to `const a = await run(1, good); const b = await run(0, under);`. Verified GREEN.
prd.json US-002 AC5 -- same shape as US-001 AC1/US-002 AC1/AC2. Verified GREEN.
prd.json US-002 AC7 -- change `runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => ({` to `await runGates({ spawnFn: (async (c, a) => ({`. Verified GREEN.

This session made NO edits to any file (nothing to commit): the only in-scope target (prd.json's acceptanceCriteria oracle strings) is worker-write-denied, and there is no non-prd.json workaround since the defect is in the proof-of-record text itself, not in production code (scripts/check-all.ts, already fixed by US-R2-001, is unmodified and confirmed correct: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 5956 pass / 0 fail, both re-run this session with zero code changes).
nextStoryContext: US-R6-001 could not be implemented: it is a review finding whose only correct fix is editing scripts/cam/prd.json's own acceptanceCriteria oracle strings (US-001 AC1-AC3, US-002 AC1-AC5/AC7), and that file is worker-write-denied for CAM_WORKER=1 sessions by .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh (confirmed empirically). This is the same class of structural dead end already fully documented at scripts/cam/patterns.md:1058-1074 (CAM-433/CAM-434), including the explicit rule to halt with BLOCKED_QUALITY rather than narrate an 'accepted gap'. All 9 replacement oracle strings were computed AND verified GREEN against branch HEAD this session (see openQuestions above for exact text/diffs); a planner/reviewer/operator session (not CAM_WORKER-gated) should paste the 8 mechanical fixes directly and make the one judgment call on US-001 AC2's retarget, then re-flip this story or fold the edit into the next review round.
